_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES: idx 2, 4, 6 (idx 0 = bilingual cover, idx 1/3/5 = the Hindi block of the English block that follows it). The alternating hypothesis HELD exactly, with no exceptions: I checked the top of every odd page and the last page, and NONE carried English overflow — each odd page opens a fresh Hindi block (idx 1 'सामान्य निर्देश', idx 3 Hindi Q5, idx 5 the Hindi 'खण्ड ग' heading) and each English block ends flush at a question boundary, so no question spans a language break. There is no parity inversion and no English-only final page: idx 6 is the last page and is English. Page map — idx 0 cover · idx 1 Hindi instructions + Q1-Q4 · idx 2 English instructions + Q1-Q4 · idx 3 Hindi Q5-Q10 · idx 4 English Q5-Q10 · idx 5 Hindi Q11-Q14 · idx 6 English Q11-Q14. All 14 question numbers present and unbroken. STRUCTURE CONFIRMED off the cover and the printed General Instructions (idx 2): 7 printed pages, 14 questions, 40 marks, 2 hours; Section A Q1-6 @2 (12) + Section B Q7-10 @3 (12) + Section C Q11-14 @4 (16) = 40; instruction (vii) 'Question no. 14 is a case-study based question with 2 sub-parts of 2 marks each'. NO MCQs anywhere in the paper — every one of the 14 questions is subjective, so there are no options, no answer letters, and no blind key re-derivation to run. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (vi) reads 'There is an internal choice in some questions' and prints NO counts, so the count was established by walking the OFFICIAL MARKING SCHEME question by question (ms idx 2-9, which reprints each question stem and both branches where an OR exists) and cross-reading the printed 'OR' on the paper itself. FOUR internal choices — Q4, Q8, Q10, Q12 — and TEN questions with none (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q9, Q11, Q13, Q14). Both branches ingested for all four. Row count 19 = 10 single + 4x2 alternatives + 1 case study x 2 sub-parts. plan.txt says 'No reference papers given', so nothing was skipped. Marking-scheme coverage verified complete: ms idx 0-1 are the evaluator's general instructions, idx 2-9 carry A1-A14 with no question missing.

questions.stem: A bag contains 3 red and 4 white balls. Three balls are drawn at random, one-by-one without replacement from the bag. If the first ball drawn is red in colour, then find the probability that the remaining two balls drawn are also red in colour.

A coin is tossed twice. The following table shows the probability distribution of number of tails :

| X | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P(X) | K | 6K | 9K |

(a) Find the value of K.

(b) Is the coin tossed biased or unbiased ? Justify your answer.
The foot of a perpendicular drawn from the point \((-2, -1, -3)\) on a plane is \((1, -3, 3)\). Find the equation of the plane.
If \(|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}|^2 = 400\) and \(|\vec{b}| = 5\), then find the value of \(|\vec{a}|\).
Find all the possible vectors of magnitude \(5\sqrt{3}\) which are equally inclined to the coordinate axes.

Find the general solution of the differential equation

\(\sec^2 x \cdot \tan y \, dx + \sec^2 y \cdot \tan x \, dy = 0.\)

questions.stem: Find the area of the region \(\{(x, y) : x^2 \le y \le x + 2\}\), using integration.

questions.subtopic: Definite Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem

questions.stem: If \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\) are mutually perpendicular vectors of equal magnitude, then prove that the vector \((2\vec{a} + \vec{b} + 2\vec{c})\) is equally inclined to both \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{c}\). Also, find the angle between \(\vec{a}\) and \((2\vec{a} + \vec{b} + 2\vec{c})\).

If a line makes \(60^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\) angles with the positive directions of x-axis and z-axis respectively, then find the angle that it makes with the positive direction of y-axis. Hence, write the direction cosines of the line.
questions._flag: OFFICIAL KEY IS INCOMPLETE (not wrong) — a finding for the solution-authoring step, not something to resolve here. The marking scheme correctly derives \(m^2 = 1/4 \Rightarrow m = \pm 1/2\) and then reports only \(\theta = 60^\circ\) with direction cosines \(\langle 1/2, 1/2, 1/\sqrt{2} \rangle\), silently dropping the \(m = -1/2\) branch (angle \(120^\circ\), direction cosines \(\langle 1/2, -1/2, 1/\sqrt{2} \rangle\)), which the printed stem admits just as much. Marking scheme page idx 6.

questions.stem: Check whether the lines \(\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4}\) and \(\dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = z\) are skew or not.

Find the equations of the planes passing through the line of intersection of the planes \(\vec{r} \cdot (\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) = 6\) and \(\vec{r} \cdot (3\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}) = 0\), which are at a distance of 1 unit from the origin.
Find the particular solution of the differential equation \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y + \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} = 0\), given that \(y(1) = 0\).

Find the general solution of the differential equation

\(x (y^3 + x^3) \, dy = (2y^4 + 5x^3 y) \, dx.\)

questions.context:
In a game of Archery, each ring of the Archery target is valued. The centremost ring is worth 10 points and rest of the rings are allotted points 9 to 1 in sequential order moving outwards.

Archer A is likely to earn 10 points with a probability of \(0{\cdot}8\) and Archer B is likely the earn 10 points with a probability of \(0{\cdot}9\).

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :

If both of them hit the Archery target, then find the probability that
questions.stem: exactly one of them earns 10 points.
questions._figure: DECORATIVE — the printed archery-target illustration (page idx 6) only labels the rings '1 point' to '10 points', which the passage already states in words. Both probabilities needed (0·8, 0·9) are in the stem text. Not attached.
questions._flag: PRINTED AS-IS: the passage reads 'Archer B is likely the earn 10 points' where 'to earn' is meant. Transcribed faithfully. This is CBSE's own typesetting error, not a render artefact — the official marking scheme (page idx 9) reprints the passage with the identical wording.
